html:
The Mokaná are an Indigenous people of the Atlántico department on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, near Barranquilla and the mouth of the Magdalena River. They are the only Indigenous community in the department.

Before the Spanish arrived they lived in farming and fishing villages between the river and the sea, neighbours of the Zenú to the southwest. Spanish rule from the 1500s brought them under colonial towns and estates, and their language, part of the Malibu family, has died out; only a few hundred words survive. Their descendants have reclaimed their identity in recent decades.
